changeSet.author: nico
changeSet.comment:
RSDEV-1326: index DigitalObjectIdentifier on (type, identifier). The PIDINST lookup asks "is this PID already linked here?" for a whole page of provider hits at once, and the table carried an index only on publicLink, so every one of those was a full scan of a table that grows with every IGSN ever allocated, bulk allocations included.
Written as raw SQL rather than createIndex because the identifier column needs a prefix length, which Liquibase's createIndex cannot express (createIndex plus modifySql/replace would, at the cost of being harder to read than the statement itself). 190 characters of utf8mb4 is 760 bytes, under the 767-byte PER-COLUMN prefix limit of the REDUNDANT and COMPACT row formats a long-lived deployment may still be using - the total key length is a separate 3072-byte budget this is nowhere near. The full 255 would be 1020 bytes on the column and would fail there. DOIs and Handles are far shorter than 190, so nothing loses discrimination.
The prefixed part must come last, which is what forces the order rather than mere tidiness: a prefixed key part cannot be seen through, so any part positioned after it is unusable. (identifier(190), type) would leave type dead weight; this way both parts work, with type taking the equality match and identifier the IN over the page.
deleted is left out because (type, identifier) already narrows to about one row and the query selects whole entities, so a prefix index can never cover it and the row fetch happens regardless - deleted in the key would buy nothing. That holds while soft-deleted duplicates of one (type, identifier) stay few, which ADR 0009 accepts. Neither query can satisfy its ORDER BY id from this index either, so a small filesort remains in both.
ALGORITHM=INPLACE, LOCK=NONE is stated rather than left to the default so MariaDB fails loudly if some future row format or engine setting cannot add the index without copying the table, instead of silently rebuilding it while the application is starting.
